gaps.fact: Galicia is also known as Green Spain. The name appears nowhere in the Codex (the chapter says the green granite northwest), and the same Court term returns in the País Vasco climate cell of Spain: Other DOs.
Rías Baixas means low estuaries, the lower rías. The chapter and article teach the drowned inlets but never translate the name.
Albariño is made with modern technology in stainless steel tanks. Only the article says so; no chapter fact or stem gives the steel, and the lees ageing is asked only of Godello.

Valdeorras makes red wine from Mencía as well as white Godello; Ribeira Sacra makes white wine from Albariño and Godello as well as red Mencía. The Village chapter gives one grape per DO and no stem asks the second colour; only the grape profiles list the regions.

Granbazán and Lagar de Cervera, two of the Court's three Albariño houses, appear nowhere in the Codex; Pazo Señorans stands only in the article and the producer entry, and no stem in either bank asks a Galician producer.

notes: Mapped questions: Régionale 59 (Spain), Village 37 (Spain), 96 in all; both categories carry every Spanish subject, and by stem the Galician share is 5 Régionale (i-xpt7m2ad, i-atdsnx4m, i-gkdh9pzb, i-fqj9q1nw, i-orbo72fi) and 4 Village (c-zlo7e9pm, c-j64y21pw, c-f5pw6pll, c-5a4c7iec). Beyond the map: Geography & Maps places Rías Baixas twice (i-0x24pbu4, i-9d2glgqc), Portugal asks Alvarinho and the Minho pergolas (i-ejw6r08q, i-uw8dxjvz), and the atlas carries eight Rías Baixas region questions. Galicia is well taught for its Introductory column: Albariño, the pergola, the 100 per cent label rule and the Atlantic climate all have stems. The thin cells are Certified: granite is a Régionale chapter phrase and an article line but no stem asks it; the second colour of each inland DO; and two of the three producers. The Codex spells the Court's Pazo Señorans as Pazo de Señoráns in the article and Pazo de Señorans in the producer entry; the Court prints the label form. No errors found. One search spent: the Rías Baixas specification was consolidated in July 2024 and Ribeira Sacra's amended by a resolution of 7 February 2025 (published in the EU journal on 28 May 2025); neither touches a cell the Court prints (the Albariño 100 per cent rule and the grapes of Valdeorras and Ribeira Sacra stand), so nothing is logged as a court update. Valdeorras showed no change. Card, fact and trap numbers count from one.
